summary_paragraph: A woman with advanced AIDS (CD4 22, high viral load, not yet restarted on antiretroviral therapy), ESRD from HIVAN on thrice-weekly hemodialysis via tunneled femoral catheter, chronic right V1 post-herpetic neuralgia/headache, eosinophilia, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was admitted after an episode of profound weakness and lightheadedness with one episode of non-bloody emesis shortly after dialysis, accompanied by hypotension. Given severe immunocompromise and low blood pressures, she initially received IV fluids and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics; chest X-ray showed no acute process, lactate improved with fluids, and she remained afebrile without localizing infectious symptoms, with blood cultures showing no growth by discharge, so antibiotics were stopped. Her symptoms improved after discontinuation of recently started pregabalin (Lyrica), felt to be the most likely cause. She continued scheduled hemodialysis and opportunistic infection prophylaxis (TMP-SMX and azithromycin), received medication reconciliation and counseling due to low health literacy, and was started on low-dose duloxetine three times weekly after dialysis for neuropathic pain. She was discharged home with services with instructions to avoid pregabalin, monitor for recurrent dizziness, and follow closely with her HIV and dialysis teams, including support for restarting antiretroviral therapy using blister packs and outpatient psychiatry follow-up for depressed mood.
